title: Mirabel and the Summer
premise: Cellist Emrys Marchetti, twenty years after a catastrophic final performance ended her concert career, teaches music in a fading coastal town and measures her life in small safe steps. When a snowstorm strands her with Theo Vance — her conservatory rival and the man who witnessed her collapse — old wounds and old love resurface, complicated further by an unexpected inheritance: a crumbling summer house left to both of them by the teacher who once believed in them both. As they restore the house through one long summer, Emrys must decide whether the careful life she built is a refuge or a cage, and whether she can risk the stage — and Theo — again. The story ends at the season's last ferry: Emrys boards it not to flee, but to play again in London, with Theo beside her, having chosen both the music and the man.
about_author: Mirabel Oyelaran is a former orchestral librarian who grew up in ferry towns and writes love stories about second chances and the houses that hold them. She lives within sight of the sea and still cannot pass a music shop without going in.

chapters.title: The Winter Set
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Twenty years after her collapse, Emrys teaches cello in a coastal town, her life deliberately small. A student's recital triggers a panic attack she hides. Beat: the cage she built is comfortable, but cracking.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Driving home from a conference, she's caught in a snowstorm and forced into a rural inn where the only other stranded guest is Theo Vance, her conservatory rival. Beat: the past walks in wearing a wool coat.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, now a famous conductor, recognizes her instantly. Over inn whiskey, they circle the night of her final performance — the one he witnessed and never explained. Beat: old resentment, new curiosity.

chapters.title: The Mistake
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Snowbound for three days, walls erode. They argue, laugh, and finally sleep together — the best mistake of their twenties, repeated at forty. Beat: reckless warmth against the cold.

chapters.title: Morning, Melting
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Roads clear; Theo leaves for a tour without saying goodbye properly, leaving only a phone number. Emrys tells herself it meant nothing. Beat: retreat into safety.

chapters.title: Solicitor's Letter
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A letter arrives: her old mentor Ida Solheim has died, leaving a summer house jointly to Emrys and Theo. Beat: grief and disbelief — Ida chose to bind them together.

chapters.title: The House on the Point
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She visits the decaying house, full of Ida's sheet music and a locked room. Theo arrives, equally stunned. Beat: two rivals, one inheritance, no escape.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They draft an agreement: fix the house over summer, sell it, split proceeds, never speak of the inn. Beat: a contract built to keep feelings out.

chapters.title: First Repairs
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They begin repairs, bickering over paint and methods, discovering Ida's annotations in old scores. Beat: grudging rhythm forms between them.

chapters.title: The Locked Room
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They open Ida's locked room: reviews of Emrys's catastrophic concert, letters, and an unfinished composition titled 'For the Girl Who Stopped.' Beat: Ida never stopped believing in her.

chapters.title: What Theo Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Emrys demands the truth about that night. Theo admits he saw her hands shaking before she did and said nothing, ashamed — and has carried it since. Beat: confession, but not absolution.

chapters.title: Summer Arrives
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Tourists return; her students beg her to play at the town festival. She refuses. Theo watches her say no. Beat: the safe life reasserts itself.

chapters.title: Ferry Schedules
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo extends his stay, canceling a conducting engagement, claiming house repairs. His agent warns his career can't wait. Beat: he starts choosing her, quietly.

chapters.title: Ida's Letters
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Letters reveal Ida's own abandoned career and her regret at never returning to the stage. 'The house is not a monument,' Ida wrote. 'It is a door.' Beat: the inheritance reframed.

chapters.title: The Neighbor's Orchard
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Warm domestic chapter: neighbors, jam-making, a village dinner where Theo and Emrys are mistaken for a married couple and don't correct it. Beat: found family begins to form.

chapters.title: Duet
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds a cello in the barn and asks her to play. She refuses. He plays piano instead, badly, until she corrects his fingering — her hands remembering. Beat: music as seduction.

chapters.title: The Student
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Her gifted student Priya asks Emrys to accompany her at the festival. Emrys says no; Priya is crushed. Theo calls her a coward. Beat: the cage visibly hurting someone else.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A summer storm damages the roof; the town rallies to help, revealing how deeply the community has adopted them both. Beat: belonging she didn't ask for.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the repaired porch, they nearly kiss; Emrys pulls back, citing the contract. Theo, frustrated, almost leaves. Beat: tension at its highest since the inn.

chapters.title: The Review
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She finds Ida's copy of the review that destroyed her — and Ida's marginalia dismantling it line by line. Beat: the verdict of twenty years begins to overturn.

chapters.title: Midsummer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the village bonfire, she and Theo finally kiss properly, contract be damned. Beat: surrender to the summer.

chapters.title: Happy, Briefly
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A golden stretch: mornings of repairs, evenings of music, Priya's lessons with both of them. Beat: the life neither dared plan for.

chapters.title: The Agent's Call
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's agent offers him a dream post in London — starting in September. He hasn't told Emrys. Beat: the choice he hoped to avoid.

chapters.title: Priya's Audition
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Priya secretly enters a conservatory audition and needs an accompanist. Emrys agrees to rehearse with her — but only behind closed doors. Beat: teaching as rehearsal for her own return.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She finds a photo of herself at nineteen with Ida and young Theo, radiant mid-phrase. She plays Ida's unfinished piece alone at midnight. Beat: grief and hunger intertwined.

chapters.title: Overheard
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys overhears Theo's call accepting the London post — and assumes he's leaving her out of it. She doesn't confront him; she withdraws. Beat: the oldest wound reopening.

chapters.title: Cold Rooms
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo senses her retreat but misreads it as regret over the inn. Both retreat into the contract's language. Beat: miscommunication hardening into distance.

chapters.title: The Festival
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Priya performs; her accompanist falls ill. The town looks to Emrys. She freezes backstage, twenty years collapsing. Beat: the crisis point.

chapters.title: Hands
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds Emrys mid-panic and does what he failed to do at twenty-two: he stays, grounds her, tells her the shaking was never the failure — the stopping was. Beat: the truth that heals.

chapters.title: She Plays
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Shaking, Emrys walks out and accompanies Priya — her first public performance in two decades. The town weeps. Beat: the wall breaks open.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Euphoria and terror. Theo confesses about London and asks her to come. Emrys, raw, accuses him of deciding for her — again. Beat: love and anger colliding.

chapters.title: The Empty Side of the Bed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo leaves to settle London logistics, giving her space she didn't want. The house feels like a museum again. Beat: the cost of safety, fully priced.

chapters.title: Ida's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In the locked room she finds Ida's final letter: the house goes wholly to whoever has the courage to stay — and to whoever has the courage to leave. Beat: the inheritance's true terms revealed.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A London orchestra, having heard of the festival, invites Emrys to audition for a principal cello chair — the same week as the last ferry. Beat: everything arrives at once.

chapters.title: What the House Is For
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys decides to keep the house as a summer music school for Priya and children like her — a found family with a roof. Beat: the door, not the monument.

chapters.title: The Argument at the Point
chapters.summary: Emrys and Theo, alternating POV. Theo returns; they fight about protection, pride, and twenty years of deciding for each other — then finally say the true things. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Audition
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys travels to London and plays Ida's finished piece — completed by her own hand — for the panel. Beat: the performance she owed herself.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The final ferry departs at dusk. Emrys stands at the rail as the town shrinks — and Theo is aboard beside her; he chose the smaller post near her, and she let him choose. Beat: departure as arrival.

chapters.title: September
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. London: a small flat, a big chair, Sunday ferries home. Theo conducts; Emrys plays; they keep Ida's house alive each summer. Beat: the new ordinary, chosen.

chapters.title: For the Girl Who Stopped
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the school's first summer concert, Emrys performs Ida's composition with Priya and the town listening, and dedicates it aloud. Beat: memory honored, inheritance accepted, love at rest.
